messages.author: 4d992ac005b751e4
messages.subject: using GPU for Nimble?
parts:
Hello everyone,
At the risk of asking a silly question, do some of you use the GPU instead of the CPU for their calculation, and is it possible on Nimble and more generally on R? 
If so, are the computation times really interesting? 
I read some stuff on it but it's not very clear to me. Indeed, my graphics card is an AMD Firepro, and I understand that this can obly be done with NVIDIA. Do you have any information to give me on the subject?
I thank you in advance
Ugoline

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: using GPU for Nimble?
parts:
Hi Ugoline,

It's not possible to use a GPU with NIMBLE at the moment. We're exploring some possibilities in this area, so we're hoping it will be feasible in the future.

In general in R there are some packages that allow you to transfer computation to the GPU -  see here under the GPU section: https://cran.r-project.org/web/views/HighPerformanceComputing.html.  Many of those probably do indeed require an NVIDIA card. You might also see the tensorflow package for R. This allows one to do computations through tensorflow, which supports computation on a GPU.

-chris
